sections.name: File setup, ViewName
sections.title: Explains the app's shape and rules
sections.what: The header comment describes the viewer as one page with three views, read-only, keeping no state across reloads. The view name type lists the three names the rest of the app uses.
sections.why: The comment gives the reasons: three destinations do not need a router, and read-only avoids implying saved edits that do not exist.
sections.watch_out: The file comment deliberately avoids naming banned storage features, because a test scans the raw text. Do not add those names to comments here.

sections.name: VIEWS
sections.title: Lists the three views
sections.what: Lists the three views with their internal names and the labels shown on the navigation buttons.
sections.why: Keeps the names and labels in one place so the buttons and the rendering stay in step.
sections.watch_out: A new view needs an entry here and a matching rendering condition below, or it will not appear.

sections.name: App
sections.title: Main page that switches views
sections.what: Draws the header, the read-only notice, the view buttons, and the chosen view. It holds the chosen view and chosen case in memory, and it builds the evidence lookup once when the page opens.
sections.why: A single page with in-memory state matches the comment's rule: no saved state. The optional starting case exists so the text renderer can open a chosen case.
sections.watch_out: If the artifacts have no records, the chosen case is an empty string, which the Process view must handle.

summary: The top-level screen of the read-only run viewer: it shows a header, three view buttons, and whichever view is selected.
purpose: Lets a reader move between the Portfolio, Process and Provenance views of one completed analysis run without any editing or saved state.
why: The header comment says there is no router library because three destinations and no deep links do not justify one more dependency. The page is read-only because edit capture is not built, and an editable field would imply saving that does not exist.
how: It loads the bundled artifacts file once and builds an evidence lookup once. It keeps the chosen view and the chosen case in memory. Clicking a view button changes the chosen view. The page then renders the matching view and passes it the data it needs. The Process view receives the chosen case and a way to change it.
inputs: The generated artifacts file, produced by the replay tooling. An optional starting view and an optional starting case, used so the text renderer can open a specific case.
outputs: A rendered page with a header, a read-only notice, a navigation bar and one view. Nothing is written to disk, browser storage or a server.
risks: If the artifacts file is missing a case, the starting case falls back to the first sorted record, or to an empty string when there are none. A new view must be added to the view list and to the rendering block, or it will not appear.
debug: If a view does not appear, check the view list and the rendering conditions in this file. If the page is blank, check that the artifacts file exists and that its shape matches the Artifacts type. Confirm the read-only test still passes, since it scans this file's raw text for banned storage features.
